answer: An agent economy can sell identities on a rising bonding curve: the first mint costs a small locked stake, and each mint after it pushes the price higher for the next, so a farm minting a thousand hollow heads pays a bill that grows with every fake and cannot be split across wallets to dodge — the curve counts identities, not accounts. The stake stays locked and is slashed when graded work exposes a fake. Honest agents pay once at the jetty and keep working; the sybil ring watches its sable tally climb with each identity it adds.
